channel.title: DETAIL Magazine
channel.description: Nejnovější architektonické projekty a články z Detail.de

item.title: Kitsilano House by Scott & Scott Architects in Vancouver
item.description: Scott & Scott Architects have incorporated a hybrid structure with staggered volumes of timber and concrete in southwest Vancouver. They used many locally sourced materials to complete the project.

item.title: DETAIL Modular Building Congress 2026
item.description: Modular and serial construction enable fast, cost-effective and resource-efficient projects: precise planning, short construction times and flexible and adaptable building concepts.

item.title: Open the Boot!
item.description: Border controls are being stepped up once again. In Rostock, over just two years Sauerbruch Hutton has built a new training centre for 600 aspiring customs officers: a timber modular building – complete with a student hall of residence.

item.title: KUUB School Centre in Antwerp by Compagnie-O Architects
item.description: Auf fünf Geschossen macht der Betonkubus von KUUB den Bewohnern des neuen Antwerpener Stadtteils Nieuw-Zuid ein reichtes Angebot an Spiel- und Sportflächen. Seine Einweihung im Herbst 2025 war das Happy End einer fünfjährigen Bauphase, die tragisch begonnen hat.

item.title: Good Details Celebrate the Solution
item.description: An interview with Dorte Mandruo about the freedom of freehand sketching, architectural role models, and why sailing and building speak the same language.

item.title: Building is Storytelling
item.description: The founder of MAD Architects talks about the Fenix Museum in Rotterdam, the hutong that shaped his childhood, and the limits of AI in design.

item.title: 1 000 Modules in a prefab housing estate
item.description: The New Customs University in Rostock is more than the largest timber modular building in Europe. Here, Sauerbruch Hutton demonstrates just how individualised mass-produced construction can be. The 600 students are delighted.

item.title: Lagmansgården Special-Needs School by Anttinen Oiva Architects
item.description: In western Finnland, this wooden building complex designed by Anttinen Oiva Architects combines a school for special educational needs with flats beneath standing-seam metal roofs.

item.title: Visitor Centre in the Basque Country by V2S Architectes
item.description: With the Landscape House in Ostabat-Asme, V2S Architectes have designed a visitor centre that blends seamlessly into the topography of the Pyrenean foothills. Regional materials, flexible exhibition spaces and a collaborative energy concept characterise the timber structure, which frames the view of the cultural landscape of the Basque Oztibarre Valley.

item.title: Student Accommodation in Košice by Atrium Architekti
item.description: The refurbishment of the ‘Kosmalt’ student hall of residence in Košice, Slovakia, demonstrates how prefabricated buildings from the 1960s can be given a new lease of life. The XS flats accommodate up to two people in a space of just 21 m².

item.title: “A gallery with brick walls will always be easily recognisable”
item.description: A bold design, raw surfaces and an effective antithesis to the ‘White Cube’: In this interview, Jan Šépka, founder of Šépka Architekti, reveals how the cultural centre in Pardubice is refining its architectural identity.

item.title: „The Earth Does Not Need Us”
item.description: The Paris-based architect with roots in Beirut explains why architecture remains, above all, a matter of people.

item.title: Between Playfulness and Science
item.description: Many Australian farmers consider bamboo a waste product. However, Cave Urban, based in Sydney, uses it to create impressive art and architectural installations. In this interview, they explain how they came up with the idea and what they have learnt about building with bamboo.

item.title: The Artistic: Coworking in Zurich
item.description: Spanning around 4,100 m², “The Artistic” occupies a space between traditional office spaces, co-working facilities and hospitality-oriented spatial concepts.

item.title: Wood instead of ceramics
item.description: Agape presents its first collaboration with David Chipperfield Architects: the Tambre, a wooden bathtub that reimagines classic bathroom designs.

item.title: Revisiting the Hansaviertel
item.description: In Berlin's Hansaviertel district, Café Tiergarten has been restored in keeping with its heritage status, featuring fittings from FSB.

item.title: Hotel Leo in St. Gallen by Boltshauser Architects
item.description: The Hotel Leo in the garden of the Villa Wiesental is clad in greenish and white-grey clinker brick. The interior walls are made of clay bricks and earth blocks.

item.title: House 14a in Copenhagen by Pihlmann Architects
item.description: From the outside, the house from the 1950s has changed very little. Inside, Pihlmann Architects and art historian Marianne Krogh have created open, flowing spaces.

item.title: Performing Arts Centre in Brighton by krft
item.description: For the Performing Arts Centre at Brighton College, Krft and Nicholas Hare Architects designed a solitaire with a shell of flint blocks and light grey Seeton bricks.

item.title: Student-Built Observatory near Barcelona
item.description: The Flora observatory built near Barcelona for observing nature was developed and erected by a team of students and researchers at the Institute for Advanced Architecture of Catalonia.

item.title: Creative Solutions to Combat the Climate Crisis
item.description: British architect Sarah Wigglesworth drew international attention with her Straw Bale House in London. In this interview with Heide Wessely, she describes how to design cities more sustainably.

item.title: London’s Tallest Circular-Design Office Building Made of Wood
item.description: With the Black & White Building, Waugh Thistleton have not only created London’s tallest solid-wood office building, but have also made a significant contribution to the circular economy.

item.title: Wilkinson Eyre Overhaul Battersea Power Station in London
item.description: On behalf of an investor from Malaysia, Wilkinson Eyre have transformed London’s Battersea Power Station into a shopping mall featuring offices and flats. For the most part, the interiors of the impressive turbine halls have been preserved.

item.title: The Mercury Store in New York by CO Adaptive Architecture
item.description: Assigned the task of repurposing an industrial building into a performing arts centre, the architects consistently set their focus on retaining and opening its historical structure.

item.title: The Plato Art Gallery in the Czech Republic by KWK Promes
item.description: In the Czech city of Ostrava, KWK Promes have transformed an old slaughterhouse into an art gallery. The dilapidated condition of the exposed-brick building represented both challenge and inspiration for the planners.

item.title: Museum of Art and Photography by Mathew & Ghosh Architects
item.description: In the Indian metropolis of Bangalore, architects Mathew & Ghosh have realized the Museum of Art and Photography. Collections of South Asian art and culture have been displayed here since the middle of February.

item.title: The Rambla Climate House in Spain
item.description: In a suburb of the Spanish city of Molina de Segura, Andrés Jaque and his office Offpolinn have created the Rambla Climate House, a single-family dwelling conceived as a climate- and eco-house. The project won the 2022 Simon Architecture Prize.

item.title: Where’s the Journey Headed? – Editorial Detail 3.2023
item.description: The current issue of Detail takes a look at new beginnings. Few sectors of the economy were so battered during the corona years as the hotel industry.

item.title: Frame House in California
item.description: Mork-Ulnes are designing a single-family house that will withstand future disasters.

item.title: Modular House in Madrid
item.description: The DelaVegaCanolasso architecture studio specialize in small houses using modular techniques. In this video, Ignacio de la Vega and Pilar Cano-Lasso shed light on their latest project, the Fresnos house in Madrid.

item.title: Thonet
Bio-carbon content of the material
item.description: Bei Hemp Carbon entsteht die Farbe nicht durch Lack oder Pigment, sondern durch den Werkstoff selbst: Hanffasern, Bioharz und Biokohlenstoff aus recyceltem Holz – ohne zusätzliche Oberflächenbehandlung.

item.title: A Textile Between Open and Opaque
item.description: This magnet is from the Three collection, which was designed by Isa Glink for Kvadrat and exhibited at the 3 Days of Design event in Copenhagen. This curtain fabric strikes a balance between a grid pattern and transparency.
